summary.text: The Maunder Minimum was a stretch from about 1645 to 1715 when sunspots became extremely rare.
Between 1672 and 1699 observers saw fewer than 50 sunspots, compared with the 40,000–50,000 typical of a similar span in modern times.
It fell within the cold Little Ice Age, but that cooling began earlier and is thought to stem mainly from volcanic activity, so any link to the quiet Sun is still being evaluated.

facts.label: Name popularised by
facts.value: John A. Eddy, in a 1976 Science paper

facts.label: Isotope evidence
facts.value: Carbon-14 and beryllium-10 show lower solar activity

items.prompt: In modern times, a span of about 28 years shows tens of thousands of sunspots. How many were recorded in the 28 years from 1672 to 1699?

options.label: About 20,000
About 5,000
Fewer than 50
About 45,000

items.explain: Fewer than 50 sunspots were seen in 1672–1699, against the 40,000–50,000 typical of a similar modern span.

items.prompt: A friend says the quiet Sun of the Maunder Minimum caused the Little Ice Age. What is the best reply?

options.label: Right: the Sun alone set off the whole cold spell
Unlikely: cooling began earlier, and volcanoes lead
Wrong: the quiet Sun made Europe much warmer
Wrong: the Little Ice Age only began after 1715

items.explain: The Little Ice Age began well before the Maunder Minimum, and its best-supported cause is volcanic activity, so a quieter Sun was not the main driver.

items.prompt: Besides old counts of sunspots, what kind of record also shows the Sun was less active during this period?

options.label: Carbon-14 and beryllium-10 stored in tree rings and ice
Sea temperatures written down in ships' logbooks
Ages of fresh craters found on the Moon
Pollen grains preserved in old lake mud

items.explain: Carbon-14 and beryllium-10, kept in reservoirs such as ice sheets and tree rings, record past solar activity and indicate it was lower then.

items.prompt: Witnesses of the 1706 solar eclipse saw the Sun's outer atmosphere, the corona, during this quiet period. What did it look like?

options.label: Bright, with long streamers
Deep red and shaped like a ring
Weak and without structure
Larger and brighter than usual

items.explain: Eye-witness reports and paintings of the 1706 eclipse show a weak, structureless corona, matching models for low magnetic flux.

items.prompt: Was the Maunder Minimum a one-off event in the Sun's history?

options.label: Yes, nothing like it has been found in any record
No, it repeats every 11 years with each solar cycle
Yes, apart from one similar spell in ancient Rome
No, about 18 quiet spells appear in 8,000 years

items.explain: Other minima such as the Spörer and Dalton Minima are known, and there seem to have been 18 such periods in the last 8,000 years.

items.prompt: A 2011 study looked at how low solar activity relates to winter weather through the jet stream. What did it find?

options.label: Winters got colder by the same amount everywhere
Some regions got colder winters, others milder ones
Winters got milder across the whole Northern Hemisphere
Winter weather showed no link to the Sun at all

items.explain: Low solar activity was linked to jet stream behavior that brought mild winters to southern Europe and Canada/Greenland but colder ones to northern Europe and the US.
